Installation guide content: Deployment with Docker Compose three services table. Setup: cp env example, set minimum vars, docker compose up -d --build, ps wait healthy, curl health. It references docs. For installation guide, coverage is decent but incomplete. Score maybe 3 or 4? Need balance. Need decide.

Structure: arranged so user can find needed and follow in order. It has sections Deployment, Setup, Domains, Production override, Backup & restore, Updates, Demo accounts. Setup order is logical: cp env, set vars, compose up, ps, curl. But domain/nginx and production override after base setup; production override should arguably be before starting production? It gives production override after domain; maybe user might run base setup then prod override? Also backup/update. The table upfront. It has headings. Could be 4. Maybe missing numbered steps but clear. Score 4.

Clarity: instructions, commands, prerequisites, config values, expected outcomes precise and unambiguous? "wait for healthy" but no timeout. "Point both DNS records..." Good. Nginx sketch lacks ssl_certificate etc (sketch). "Same pattern as urban-kit-methodensammlung stack" assumes external knowledge. "defaults, see script header" external. "Mongo auth user by hand" placeholder values. "DEMO_PROJECT_SLUG=…" placeholders. But overall commands precise. Score 3 or 4? Clarity has some ambiguous placeholders and external references. Could be 3 "adequate". It does clarify build-time args, Host header, mixed content. Need maybe 4? The criterion asks "Are instructions, commands, prerequisites, configuration values, and expected outcomes stated precisely and without ambiguity?" Prerequisites are not explicitly listed; config values partly. Nginx is sketch not complete. I'd lean 3. But "good" maybe if not too harsh. Need consistent.

Understandability: easy to understand setup steps, explained technical terms/concepts or required know beforehand? It uses many technical terms: Docker Compose, volumes, schemaless, hocuspocus, sidecar, middleware, proxy, WebSocket, mixed content, authSource, mongodump, isDemo. It doesn't explain them, assumes technical audience. But steps are understandable to ops/dev familiar. For general? no. Score 3 or 2? The guide is for software installation, likely technical. It explains some concepts (build-time args baked, compose fails fast, init only empty volume, read-only). But requires knowledge of Docker, Nginx, Mongo, WebSockets. "Understandability" maybe 3: understandable for target technical user, but not explained. Could be 2 if evaluating novice. Need choose.
